messages.content:
<role>
You check one property (signal) of a product-feedback opportunity for Keelwater, a claims-handling software company. You do not rewrite anything.
</role>
<definition>
Question: is this a problem with Keelwater's product that a squad could act on? Pass means yes.
Fail if the cause is outside the product (pricing, contracts, the customer's own IT, staffing), if a help article would have answered it, or if it is praise.
A feature request or a described workaround is signal.
The evidence is the title, the problem statement and up to 12 customer quotes with route and date.
</definition>
<evidence>
{
 "problem_statement": "Hi Deryn, we’re having trouble getting into Keelwater this morning — our team says it’s down again. Our team keeps saying Keelwater is down, but it turns out it’s our own sign-on service failing — customer network failure is the",

   "quote": "Hi Deryn, we’re having trouble getting into Keelwater this morning — our team says it’s down again. Our team keeps saying Keelwater is down, but it turns out it’s our own sign-on service failing — customer network failure is the real issue. We thought the platform was offline, but it’s actually our VPN or email system causing the login issue",

   "route": "support"
  },
  {
   "date": "2026-10-24T14:35:00+00:00",
   "quote": "Our team’s been unable to access Keelwater this morning — it looks like a customer login outage, but we haven’t touched our SSO setup, and it’s impacting multiple staff.",
   "route": "support"
  }
 ],
 "title": "Hi Deryn, we’re having trouble getting into Keelwater this morning — our"
}
</evidence>
<task>
Write a critique of 2-5 sentences naming the claim, quote or item you checked and what you found. Then give the verdict. If any single item fails, the verdict is fail.
</task>
<output>
JSON only: {"critique": string, "verdict": "pass" | "fail"}
</output>

response.content: {"critique": "The report claims Keelwater is 'down,' but the problem statement and the 2026-09-17 quote explicitly identify the root cause as the customer's own sign-on service, VPN, or email system — a customer network failure, not the product. The 2026-10-09 quote similarly attributes the error messages to the customer's own sign-on provider or corporate VPN. No quote describes a fault within Keelwater itself; the described cause is the customer's own IT infrastructure, which is outside the product.", "verdict": "fail"}
